title: Flasque sheaves are acyclic
statement: For a flasque abelian sheaf $F$ on a topological space, $H^q(X_{\rm Zar},F)=0$ for $q>0$, in the resolution sense of [def-sc-zariski-cohomology].

proof.text: Let $0\to F\to I\to Q\to0$ be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on $X$ with $I$ injective in the abelian category of abelian sheaves on $X$. Let $\mathbb Z_X$ be the sheaf of locally constant $\mathbb Z$-valued functions, so $(X,\mathbb Z_X)$ is a ringed space. Every abelian sheaf carries a unique $\mathbb Z_X$-module structure (a locally constant $n$ acts on a section $s$ by gluing the sections $n_i s|_{U_i}$ on the opens $U_i$ where $n$ is the constant $n_i$), and every map of abelian sheaves is $\mathbb Z_X$-linear; so abelian sheaves on $X$ and $\mathbb Z_X$-modules are the same category, and $I$ is an injective $\mathbb Z_X$-module. Hence [lem-sc-ringed-space-injective-restriction-surjective], applied to $(X,\mathbb Z_X)$, gives that every restriction $I(V)\to I(U)$, $U\subseteq V$ open, is surjective: $I$ is flasque [def-sc-zariski-flasque]. Since $F$ is flasque, [lem-sc-zariski-flasque-quotient-sections] gives surjectivity $I(V)\to Q(V)$ for every open $V$; since $I$ is flasque, it also gives that $Q$ is flasque.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01EA (lemma-injective-restriction-surjective), applied to the ringed space (X, Z_X); Lemma 09SY proof

proof.text: Using enough injectives in the abelian category of sheaves on the Zariski site [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives], embed $F$ into an injective $I^0$ and repeat the construction on the successive quotient sheaves. Thus $F\to I^\bullet$ is an injective resolution whose every successive quotient is flasque, and the surjectivity in Step 1 makes the complex of sections $I^\bullet(V)$ exact in every positive degree for every open $V$.

source.place: Lemma 09SY proof, embed in an injective and iterate on the flasque quotient

proof.text: By [def-sc-zariski-cohomology], $H^q(X_{\rm Zar},F)$ is the $q$-th cohomology of the global-sections complex of an injective resolution. Applying the exactness from Step 2 at the object $X$ gives $H^q(X_{\rm Zar},F)=0$ for every $q>0$.

source.place: Section 01FT, definition of cohomology over an object, applied to Lemma 09SY
